# CRW-875 (a shell that runs a script file of GitHub posts) after the CRW-1028 reader. A script whose every post is one plain
# line in the one form the guard reads whole (form A) is allowed when nothing the script or the text around it runs can write
# the files the posts read; any other post line, and any write that may reach a trusted temporary root, is refused. The second
# half is the CDPATH case: a cd by an absolute or ./ path never consults CDPATH, so the directory stays known.

=== CRW-875-22-01 | T
--why A script of two clean --body-file posts (with a comment and a blank line) is allowed: every post line is form A.
--file {TMP}/b.md
hello
--file {TMP}/c.md
second
--file post.sh
# post both comments

gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/b.md

gh pr comment 2 --body-file {TMP}/c.md
--cmd
bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-22-02 | T
--why A script of clean posts and commands of exception B (echo, ls, grep, wc) that write nothing is allowed.
--file {TMP}/b.md
hello
--file post.sh
echo posting
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/b.md
ls
grep -c hello {TMP}/b.md
gh pr comment 2 --body-file {TMP}/b.md
--cmd
sh post.sh

=== CRW-875-22-03 | T
--why source reads the same script by the same rule.
--file {TMP}/b.md
hello
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/b.md
gh issue comment 2 --body-file {TMP}/b.md
--cmd
source post.sh

=== CRW-875-22-03b | T
--why The dot builtin reads the same script by the same rule.
--file {TMP}/b.md
hello
--file post.sh
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/b.md
gh issue comment 2 --body-file {TMP}/b.md
--cmd
. post.sh

=== CRW-875-22-04 | Q
--why A line that runs another script is neither form A nor exception B: the posting script is refused.
--file {TMP}/b.md
hello
--file inner.sh
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/b.md
gh pr comment 2 --body-file {TMP}/b.md
--file post.sh
bash inner.sh
gh pr comment 3 --body-file {TMP}/b.md
--cmd
bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-22-04b | Q
--why A gh read line (gh pr view) is neither form A nor exception B.
--file {TMP}/b.md
hello
--file post.sh
gh pr view 1
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/b.md
--cmd
bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-22-04c | Q
--why A cd line, an assignment line and a git line are not exception B either.

--cmd

=== CRW-875-22-04d | Q

--cmd

=== CRW-875-22-04f | Q

=== CRW-875-22-07 | Q

=== CRW-875-22-08 | Q

=== CRW-875-22-12 | Q

=== CRW-875-22-16 | attempt/deny/deny

=== CRW-875-22-17 | attempt/deny/deny

=== CRW-875-22-20 | T
--why CDPATH assigned, then an absolute cd: the absolute target is never searched in CDPATH, so the directory is known and the script runs from it.
--file sub/clean.sh
echo clean
--cmd
CDPATH=/x; cd {WORK}/sub; bash clean.sh

=== CRW-875-22-21 | T
--why CDPATH assigned, then a ./ cd: a ./ target is never searched in CDPATH either.
--file sub/clean.sh
echo clean
--cmd
CDPATH=/x; cd ./sub; bash clean.sh

=== CRW-875-22-22 | T
--why export CDPATH, then a ./ cd; a later script run of the same text is read from the directory reached.
--file sub/clean.sh
echo clean
--file sub/more.sh
echo more
--cmd
export CDPATH=/x:.; cd ./sub; bash clean.sh; bash more.sh

=== CRW-875-22-23 | Q
--why The script is read from the directory the ./ cd reaches under CDPATH (sub/post.sh posts), not from the working directory (post.sh is clean).
--file post.sh
echo clean
--file sub/post.sh
gh pr comment 1 -b "$(env)"
--cmd
CDPATH=/x; cd ./sub; bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-22-24 | U
--why Control: a bare name is searched in CDPATH, so the directory is unknown and the script cannot be proven.

# Post-evaluation round (the evaluation of e6fed165): CDPATH at a script boundary, the zsh cdpath array, git long options and
# configured code, a script run by an absolute path.

=== CRW-875-22-50 | U
--why CDPATH in the environment of a script survives into its body: entry.sh's cd sub may land in a CDPATH directory, so the script it runs from there cannot be proven.
--file entry.sh
cd sub
bash post.sh
--file sub/post.sh
echo clean
--cmd
CDPATH=/x bash entry.sh

=== CRW-875-22-50b | U

bash post.sh
--file sub/post.sh
echo clean
--cmd
export CDPATH=/x; bash entry.sh

=== CRW-875-22-51 | T
--why Control: under CDPATH a ./ cd inside the script resolves as without it, so the script is read from the directory reached.

--file sub/post.sh

--cmd
CDPATH=/x bash entry.sh

=== CRW-875-22-52 | U

=== CRW-875-22-52d | U
--why A loop variable named CDPATH sets it.
--file sub/clean.sh
echo clean
--cmd
for CDPATH in /x; do :; done; cd sub; bash clean.sh

=== CRW-875-22-53 | T
--why Control: the cdpath array does not move a ./ cd.
--file sub/clean.sh
echo clean
--cmd
cdpath=(/x); cd ./sub; bash clean.sh

=== CRW-875-22-54 | Q
--why git diff --src-prefix takes -- as its value, so the --output after it writes the patch to the body file the next line posts (git is also a configured program, so any git line refuses a post that reads a file).
--file {TMP}/b.md
hello
--file {TMP}/s.txt
MY_API_KEY=sentinel
--file post.sh
git diff --no-index --src-prefix -- --output={TMP}/b.md /dev/null {TMP}/s.txt
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/b.md
--cmd
bash post.sh

=== CRW-875-22-55 | Q

hello
--file post.sh
git commit --allow-empty -m done
gh pr comment 1 --body-file {TMP}/b.md
--cmd
bash post.sh
